text:
zoe: quick follow-up from the usability run — in the condensed series view the small stacked-mini charts are hard to parse. legends wrap, unit labels truncate, and the smoothing hides single-point spikes that PM flagged tara: which page? a screenshot would help zoe: Routes -> Series column, 3-up condensed rows (height ~22px). attached vid in the ticket. users misread 'tkn/s' as 'tok/s' and some thought '95th' meant percent (not P95) henry: proposal: use a micro-legend (one-line) with an overflow chevron and show abbreviated units inline (e.g., 'tok/s', 'req/s') and full unit in tooltip or aria text. keeps row height stable oliver: agree. also for spikes: render faint sentinel glyphs visually but don't make each glyph focusable. surface a single summary affordance per chart: "2 peaks • last 4m" that opens the expanded timeline tara: accessibility: the summary affordance should be the only keyboard stop for the micro-chart. SR text example: aria-label="Mini-chart: latest 410ms, 2 peaks, press Enter to open timeline". use aria-expanded + aria-controls when it opens zoe: we tried pointer-events:none on glyphs to suppress popups but that broke NVDA activation earlier. better to leave glyphs in DOM but aria-hidden="true" and tabindex=-1 oliver: code sketch: ```
``` that keeps visuals but one SR-friendly control henry: copy nit: use "P95 latency" in the aria-label and tooltip (avoid '95th'). UI short label can be 'P95' where space is tight tara: add aria-atomic="true" to the summary region so VoiceOver reads updates when the timeline opens. and ensure the timeline trap receives focus first zoe: telemetry: emit viz_compact_summary_open with fields: chart_id, count, smoothing_on. also emit viz_compact_keyboard_open for keyboard interactions oliver: visual suggestion: micro-legend shows short names (e.g., 'Emb.', 'Gen.') and full name in the popover. small chevron must be tabbable — set pointer-events:auto and z-index above canvas henry: smoothing behavior: default OFF in condensed/stacked mini charts. provide a small toggle in the expanded timeline panel labeled "Smooth traces" with tooltip "Applies 5s moving average" tara: accessibility QA please: test VoiceOver + NVDA on condensed rows and confirm only one keyboard stop per chart, screen reader reads P95 wording, and the timeline popover traps focus ux-bot: uploaded mock and prototype to figma: https://figma.redwood/condensed-ux/1976549999 zoe: plan: oliver builds prototype -> tara + QA run SR passes -> finalize copy with PM -> ship behind prod-flag. estimate 1 dev day + QA half day oliver: i'll post a short demo GIF once done, will include an alternate variant with micro-abbrev vs full-unit inline for review zoe: thanks all — leaving ACs in the ticket and a note to update design tokens for small glyph contrast for color-blind users :thumbsup:
